## Background

The **Australian HR Institute (AHRI)** supports HR professionals through membership, certification, training and events.

### How incoming calls reach AHRI

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 12
%%| fig-align: center
flowchart LR
    C["`**External caller**`"] -->|"Main number"| M["`**Main IVR**
Automated menu`"]

    M -->|"Service selection"| Q["`**Team queue**
Routes calls to staff`"]

    Q -->|"Call offered"| S["`**Staff phone**`"]

    C -.->|"Direct staff number"| S

    classDef main fill:#006DAE,stroke:#006DAE,color:#ffffff,font-size:22px;
    classDef light fill:#E6F0F7,stroke:#006DAE,color:#004B7A,font-size:22px;

    class M main;
    class C,Q,S light;

    linkStyle 0,1,2 stroke:#006DAE,stroke-width:2px;
    linkStyle 3 stroke:#7F8C97,stroke-width:2px;
```

::: callout-box
**The reporting gap:** email and online forms had CRM reporting. Phone activity was available mainly as raw Excel exports.
:::

::: muted
Illustrative routes: not every Main IVR call reaches a queue or a staff member. Our inbound analysis focuses on the main menu; outbound activity is analysed separately.
:::

::: notes
AHRI supports HR professionals through membership, certification, training and events.

A caller to the main number hears an automated menu. Depending on their selection and the system settings, their call may enter a team queue, where it can be offered to staff. Other calls go directly to a staff number.

The diagram illustrates the distinction between those routes. It does not establish that every call followed the entire sequence or that a person answered.

AHRI already had reporting for emails and online forms. Phone activity was mainly available in Excel exports, which motivated this dashboard.
:::

## Business problem

::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="55%"}
AHRI has no visibility and needs a clearer way to understand of

::: incremental
- **When** do members call?
- **Where** do their calls go?
- **How** do calls end, and how long do they take?
- **Who** is calling members back, and when?
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="45%"}
::: callout-box
**Our goal**

Turn the Teams phone exports into a Power BI dashboard that shows AHRI what's happening on the phones.
:::

**In scope:** inbound and outbound activity across the period of the export.<br> **Out of scope:** live reporting and individual staff performance.
::::
:::::::

## Business questions

|   | Question | Dashboard page |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Inbound | How many calls arrive, and when? | Inbound Call Overview |
| Inbound | Where do callers go? | Routing and queue destinations |
| Inbound | How do calls end, and how long do they take? | Outcome and Duration |
| Outbound | Who is making outbound calls, and when? | Outbound activity |
| Outbound | How do outbound calls end, and how long do they last? | Outbound outcome and duration |

## Data and analysis scope

Both exports cover **6 April to 1 September 2026**.

**Inbound:** one call can create several system records.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 12
%%| fig-align: center
flowchart LR
    R["`**9,859**
Inbound records`"] -->|"Group by shared ID"| G["`**6,361**
Linked call groups`"]

    G -->|"Include"| I["`**3,986**
With Main IVR`"]

    G -->|"Exclude"| D["`**2,375**
Without Main IVR`"]

    classDef source fill:#E6F0F7,stroke:#006DAE,color:#004B7A,font-size:24px;
    classDef group fill:#004B7A,stroke:#004B7A,color:#ffffff,font-size:24px;
    classDef included fill:#006DAE,stroke:#006DAE,color:#ffffff,font-size:24px;
    classDef excluded fill:#F1F3F5,stroke:#AAB3BA,color:#5F6B73,font-size:24px;

    class R source;
    class G group;
    class I included;
    class D excluded;

    linkStyle 0,1 stroke:#006DAE,stroke-width:2px;
    linkStyle 2 stroke:#7F8C97,stroke-width:2px;
```

::: {.muted style="margin-top: 0.2em;"}
Vanessa confirmed that calls without Main IVR are mostly direct to staff. We retain the 3,986 Main IVR groups and their related records. Groups do not represent unique people.
:::

::: callout-box
**Outbound scope:** 6,046 attempts by 18 approved staff across Membership, HRSC and Events.
:::

::: notes
The inbound file contains 9,859 system records. One call can generate multiple records as it moves through the system, so we group related records by their shared identifier.

This gives 6,361 linked groups. We identify the 3,986 groups with a Main IVR account record and retain their related records for the inbound analysis.

The other 2,375 groups have no Main IVR record. Vanessa confirmed that these calls are mostly direct calls to staff. They sit outside our chosen inbound scope.

These counts describe groups of records rather than unique people. Someone can call more than once.

Separately, we filter the other export to outbound calls and the 18 staff approved by AHRI. This gives 6,046 outbound attempts.
:::

## IDA and EDA: checking and exploring the data {#ida-eda}

::::::: {.columns style="font-size: 0.85em; display: flex; gap: 2em;"}
:::: {.column width="49%"}
### IDA · Check and prepare

::: muted
Initial data analysis · Power Query
:::

- **Inbound quality:** 334 missing account names and 785 missing start/end timestamps. Retained the rows with unknown values.
- **Scope:** grouped inbound rows by shared ID, selected Main IVR groups and filtered outbound to 18 approved staff.
- **Consistency:** cleaned account labels, set data types and converted UTC timestamps to Melbourne time.
::::

:::: {.column width="49%"}
### EDA · Explore patterns

::: muted
Exploratory data analysis · Power BI and DAX
:::

- **Timing:** compared daily, weekday, hourly and monthly activity, including a 7-day trailing average.
- **Routing and teams:** compared queue/overflow destinations and outbound volumes across teams.
- **Outcomes and duration:** examined technical statuses and duration bands. Compared mean and median to assess the effect of long calls.
::::
:::::::

::: muted
Weekday averages include zero-activity days and exclude boundary dates. Full-month comparisons cover May–August.
:::

::: notes
IDA means initial data analysis. We checked what each record represents, missing values, duplicates and timestamp coverage before calculating the dashboard measures.

We retained records with missing account names or timestamps because their other fields could still be useful. We did not invent replacement values. No exact duplicate inbound rows were found. Grouping related records by shared ID is therefore different from removing duplicates.

The 9,859 inbound records form 6,361 shared-ID groups, of which 3,986 contain Main IVR. Vanessa confirmed that groups without Main IVR are mostly direct calls to staff. This supported our decision to focus the inbound analysis on Main IVR. These groups are not counts of unique people.

EDA means exploratory data analysis. We used Power BI charts and DAX measures to investigate when activity occurs, which destinations and teams account for it, and how technical outcomes and recorded durations vary.

For fairer comparisons, weekday averages include zero-activity days and exclude the first and last observed dates. Public holidays remain included, and continuous coverage between the boundary dates is assumed. The trailing average covers the current day and the previous six calendar days.

These are descriptive findings. Technical success does not prove that a member spoke to staff, and recorded duration does not establish queue waiting time.
:::

## Approach

### From two Excel exports to five dashboard pages

::::::::::::: pipeline
:::: stage
::: stage-n
1
:::

**Clean**<br>Teams Direct Routing + Outbound exports; fix timestamps to Melbourne time
::::

:::: stage
::: stage-n
2
:::

**Group**<br>Used shared IDs to identify related call records: 6,361 groups, **3,986 via Main IVR**
::::

:::: stage
::: stage-n
3
:::

**Classify**<br>Main IVR, primary queue or overflow; outbound call staff mapped to 3 teams
::::

:::: stage
::: stage-n
4
:::

**Measure**<br>DAX measures for volume, routing, outcomes and duration
::::

:::: stage
::: stage-n
5
:::

**Build**<br>5 Power BI pages: 3 inbound, 2 outbound
::::
:::::::::::::

::: muted
Inbound: 6 Apr – 1 Sep 2026, calls through the Main IVR. <br> Outbound: same period, 18 staff in Membership, HRSC and Events.
:::

# Inbound Results {background-color="#006DAE"}

## Calls follow office hours, and Tuesday is the busiest day {.result}

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="72%"}
![Page 1 · Inbound calls overview](images/inbound1.png){.shot}
:::

:::: {.column width="28%"}
::: takeaways
- **3,986** calls, about **37 per weekday**
- Steady **9am–5pm**; almost nothing outside it
- **Tuesday** is busiest (\~44/day), Friday quietest (\~33)
- Weekday average fell from **\~53 in May to \~30 in August**
:::
::::
::::::

## Career Support overflows most {.result}

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="72%"}
![Page 2 · Routing and queue destinations](images/inbound2.png){.shot}
:::

:::: {.column width="28%"}
::: takeaways
- **68%** of calls show no queue record (they ended in the menu or went elsewhere)
- **Membership, Reception and Career Support** take most queue demand
- **Career Support:** \~47% of its queue calls reach overflow
- **Reception:** under 10%
:::
::::
::::::

## Most calls complete; dropped calls tend to be the long ones {.result}

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="72%"}
![Page 3 · Outcome and duration](images/inbound3.png){.shot}
:::

:::: {.column width="28%"}
::: takeaways
- \~**3,300** completed, \~**600** disconnected / timed out
- Typical call: **1.5–2 min**; average **2m 58s**
- Disconnected calls average **\~5 min**, about twice as long as completed ones
- **Career Support** has the longest queue time (**\~6.5 min**)
:::
::::
::::::

# Outbound results {background-color="#006DAE"}

## The Membership team makes almost 9 in 10 outbound calls {.result}

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="72%"}
![Page 4 · Outbound activity](images/outbound1.png){.shot}
:::

:::: {.column width="28%"}
::: takeaways
- **6,046** attempts by **18 staff**, about **57 per weekday**
- **Membership: 87%** (5,275); HRSC 680; Events 91
- Busiest **Tuesday 11am–2pm**; quietest day **Monday**
- May was the peak month (**77.8/weekday**)
:::
::::
::::::

## 91% of outbound calls connect, but most last under a minute {.result}

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="72%"}
![Page 5 · Outbound outcome and duration](images/outbound2.png){.shot}
:::

:::: {.column width="28%"}
::: takeaways
- **5,504** connected (**91%**); **542** didn't
- Main failure: **not answered** (375)
- **69%** of connected calls last **under 1 minute**; average **1:36**
- Short calls may be **voicemail**: the export can't tell us
:::
::::
::::::

## Challenge & Limitations {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Inbound

- Whether a staff member answered
- Whether a caller abandoned in the queue
- Whether the caller's question was resolved
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Outbound

- Whether the **member** answered, rather than voicemail
- The **purpose** of the call (fees, welcome, other)
- Whether the call achieved its goal
:::
